name: Tara Dean
life: “I still remember funding a chance I never got at twenty.” On Saturday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Tara takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I sponsored the trial wage. My name can stay off the winner's contract.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a rust-colored canvas coat and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Tara has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with two white streaks in otherwise dark hair. Tara gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Tara treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Tara lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To fund the trial with no obligation to the sponsor.
family: Martha Laurent is Tara’s second cousin. Tara makes the call. Martha is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A house divided kindly*, Martha says, “I am a tenant on the same street. I can't move a fence but I can share the bench I built from packing wood.”
connections: Emery Colón. Sponsor and bread customer both care whether the new job leaves a loaf ordinary workers can buy.

reactions.situation: The new baker gets the first oven slot
reactions.response: Tara makes sure the other applicant gets a comparable chance with the same oven.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Tara asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Tara says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
